title: Introduce SSE handoff sequencer and partial-JSON safety with ACK fallback
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to see customer-facing cases where SSE-streamed responses emit partial JSON spans across chunk boundaries, combined with out-of-order tool/function sentinel emission, causing downstream OpenAI-compat clients to either drop structured tool call events or block waiting for a terminal delimiter. Root cause analysis showed two contributing factors: (1) the current chunker flushes on byte/latency thresholds without awareness of atomic JSON spans and function-call sentinels; (2) transient retries/resends can replay trailing fragments that are accepted by the client as second fragments and break JSON reassembly. This PR implements a minimal, backwards-compatible runtime-side sequencer and an ACK-based fallback to make SSE emission idempotent and to preserve atomic JSON spans across chunking/replay windows. Changes in this PR are guarded behind a runtime feature-flag (sse.handoff_sequencer) and default to enabled for hosted API only until broader compatibility testing completes. Summary of approach: - Introduce a lightweight in-flight HandoffSequencer that assigns a monotonically increasing handoff_id per logical event span. Spans are the unit of atomic emission: a textual JSON object (structured output) or a function/tool sentinel plus its JSON payload. - Add an optional in-stream ACK event (event: ack) carrying the last-accepted handoff_id. ACKs are emitted by the sequencer when the final chunk for a span is flushed; clients that understand ACK can use it to resync and avoid double-applying replayed fragments. ACK events are explicitly optional for OpenAI-compatible clients: the compatibility layer will strip/translate ack events when configured. - Implement a DELIM_FALLBACK sentinel emission when a boundary is ambiguous (e.g., UTF-8 split inside a quoted string or mid-escape). This sentinel is a short single-line token that helps clients resync without waiting for a full JSON close. - Make the sequencer tolerant to transient replay by rejecting duplicate handoff_id emissions and emitting a resequence hint (event: resequence-suggest) that downstream proxies/clients may use to request a short range replay. - Preserve performance: resequencer is optimized to only buffer small windows (configurable window default 3 spans) and uses epoch-ids so memory overhead is bounded. Rollout & compatibility: - Feature flagged and enabled in hosted API rollout ring 1 only. - OpenAI-compat layer continues to expose the same textual events for clients that do not opt in; ACK and DELIM_FALLBACK are stripped or translated by the compat adapter unless client requests raw stream. - SDKs (python/ts) updated with a new opt-in stream_resync helper that understands ack/resequence hints to automatically stitch partial JSON. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for boundary detection, UTF-8 split handling, and duplicate-handling. - Integration tests in the harness that simulate retransmit/replay and confirm no double-emits. - Canary on perf lab with load-shear to check latency and p95; impact measured under 0.5% additional p50 for normal short responses. Reference tickets: ENG-8421 (design), ENG-8475 (implementation), SUP-5612 (customer incident). Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in Linear) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Backwards-compatibility verification for OpenAI-compat - [x] Canary/benchmarks - [x] Docs update (streaming semantics) Why this is different from previous fixes: Many earlier PRs focused on delimiter normalization and chunk reassembly heuristics. This change introduces an explicit handoff/sequencer abstraction and an optional in-band ACK to make handoff explicit and idempotent, reducing reliance on heuristics that are brittle under retransmit or proxy replay. The runtime continues to fall back to the old behavior when the feature flag is off. Migration notes: Enterprise Private installs should be offered the feature as opt-in via config.sse.handoff_sequencer=false until compatibility tests are completed. Support runbook and incident mitigation steps are included in docs/ops/sse-handoff-runbook.md.

review_comments: Daniel Kim (requested changes): The resequencer looks solid but we need clearer guarantees about memory bounds and what happens when handoff_id wraps. Please add epoch tagging to avoid reuse across long-lived connections.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added epoch_id and a bounded window parameter (default=3 spans) with an explicit eviction policy in sse_resequencer.py. Updated tests to cover wrap-around.
Priya Singh (nit): Can we document how SDKs should behave when ack is missing (older server)? Added doc note about fallback semantics.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added fallback note and new stream_resync helper in the Python SDK to auto-stitch without ack when possible.
Ethan Morales (approval): Verified integration test scenarios and canary perf. Approving for merge once CI green and one more test covering proxy-induced duplicate frames is added.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added proxy duplicate-frame test and pushed the fix for duplicate handoff rejection.

release_notes: Fixes multiple SSE streaming issues related to partial JSON fragments and out-of-order function/tool sentinel emission by introducing a handoff sequencer, optional ack events, and a delim-fallback sentinel. Backwards-compatible and feature-flagged. Recommended for hosted API rollout; opt-in for Private installs.
